set.descent_text: The last pitch past Table Ledge is a 5.7 traverse that exits onto Kiener's Route or the rappel route. Rappel the descent line that starts at the anchors on Table Ledge, left of the climbing: five double-rope rappels reach Broadway. Cross the loose, sloping ledge to the right to the second rappel line, which starts on Broadway beneath the Casual Route and south of North Chimney; stay well to the left on its first rappel, because slings rather than bolts mean you have strayed and the rope will stick. Four more rappels end on the snowfield; the first works on a single rope, the last three need two, and a walk around Chasm Lake returns to the trail. The alternative is to walk off: from Table Ledge, traverse left to Kiener's Route, climb it to the summit area (third class, one fourth class step), then follow cairns north to the North Face rappel from the old cable eyebolts (one double-rope or two single-rope rappels). Continue to the Boulderfield and the trail, or follow the ridge toward Mt Lady Washington and descend talus to the lake.
set.approach: Walk from the Longs Peak Trailhead, reached from Highway 7, up the Longs Peak Trail and then the Chasm Lake Trail, about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain to the lake. Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it; do not mistake the more obvious Field's Chimney for it. North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall. It gains Broadway, the ledge system across the foot of the wall. The Casual Route starts near the middle of the wall on a broken pillar of low-angle ground, which is easy to spot, and its first pitch climbs to the foot of an obvious crack.

set.descent_text: The route ends at the edge of the Diamond; one more pitch reaches a good place to unrope. Descend the North Face by third class hiking and using the rappel anchors that once held the cables. Take extreme care, especially with heavy aid gear, since a slip there drops off the other side of the peak. Continue to the Boulderfield and the trail.
set.approach: This is a big-wall aid route, so many parties avoid hauling up North Chimney, where loose rock is dangerous, and instead rappel from the Chasm View bolts, on a large detached block, to Broadway. Once on Broadway, begin right of North Chimney on the right side of the large Green Pillar, up ramps to a big right-facing dihedral.

set.descent_text: Bright Star reaches the summit by cracks and corners. From the top of the wall, go to the summit area and take the North Face (old Cables Route) down: third class, with a rappel from the anchors left from the cables (one double-rope or two single-rope rappels). Take care with a heavy pack, since a slip on the north side drops off the far side of the peak. Continue to the Boulderfield and the trail, or follow the ridge toward Mt Lady Washington and drop down a talus slope to the south into the Chasm Lake basin.
set.approach: Walk from the Longs Peak Trailhead, reached from Highway 7, up the Longs Peak Trail and then the Chasm Lake Trail, about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain to the lake. Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it; do not mistake the more obvious Field's Chimney for it. North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall. It gains Broadway, the ledge system across the foot of the wall. Bright Star starts at the left edge of the large bivouac cave on Broadway, on steep jugs leading to a clear thin crack.

set.approach: Use the usual Chasm Lake approach (Longs Peak Trailhead off Highway 7, about 4.2 miles and 2,400 ft of gain to the lake, then around the north side to North Chimney, loose fourth and low fifth class with snow early) to reach Broadway. Begin right of North Chimney at the right side of the Green Pillar, where the aid line starts.
